q: 1. Estimate is
explain: The fundamental purpose of an estimate is to calculate the probable cost of a project.

q: 2. *Which of the following is the most correct estimate?
explain: A detailed estimate is the most accurate as it involves item-by-item quantity calculations.

q: 3. A revised estimate is prepared if the sanctioned estimate exceeds
explain: A revised estimate is required whenever the actual/anticipated expenditure is likely to exceed the original sanctioned estimate by more than 5%.

q: 4. *The plinth area estimate method is also known as
explain: Because it uses the floor area (measured in square meters/feet) to calculate cost, it is also called the square rate method.

q: 5. In a detailed estimate the provision for contingencies is usually
explain: Contingencies cover minor unforeseen items/expenses and are conventionally provided at 3 to 5% of the estimated cost in a detailed estimate.

q: 6. Unit rate is only for
explain: According to the key, unit rates are used for preparing documents (like tender documents).

q: 7. The actual cost of supplementary and revised estimate is
explain: The final actual cost is only realized upon completion of the works defined in the estimates.

q: 8. *Centre-line method is used for calculation of
explain: This method is used to calculate quantities for any structure where the walls or perimeters follow a consistent center line.

q: 9. Due to change in price level, a revised estimate is prepared if the sanctioned estimate exceeds
explain: A revised estimate is required when the actual/anticipated cost exceeds the originally sanctioned estimate by more than 5%, generally due to price escalation or design changes.

q: 10. The plinth area of a building excludes
options: area of the walls at the floor level
internal shaft for sanitary installations up to 2 sq. m in area
explain: Cantilevered/projected porch areas are not covered by the building's floor slab in the conventional plinth sense and are excluded from plinth area calculation.

q: 11. Which is considered in the calculation of plinth area?
explain: Plinth area includes the wall thickness and internal circulation spaces like corridors.

q: 12. Which is not considered in the calculation of plinth area?
explain: Uncovered projections or cantilevered beams outside the wall line are excluded from the plinth area.

q: 13. While preparing a detailed estimate
options: Dimension should be measured correct to 0.01 m
Area should be measured correct to 0.01 sqm
Volume should be measured correct to 0.01 cum
explain: Standard practice requires all dimensions, areas, and volumes in a detailed estimate to be recorded correct to two decimal places (0.01) in their respective units.

q: 14. Revised estimate is warranted when the sanctioned estimate exceeds, for whether reason, by more than
explain: A revised estimate becomes necessary whenever the sanctioned estimate is exceeded by more than 5%, regardless of the reason for the excess.

q: 15. When engineering departments undertake the works of other departments the amount charged towards design, supervision and execution, etc. is called
explain: Centage charges are the percentage-based charges levied by an engineering department for providing design, supervision, and execution services to another department.

q: 16. *The plan of a building is in the form of rectangle with center line dimension of outer walls as 9.7m x 14.7m. The thickness of the wall in super structure is 0.30m. Then its carpet area is
explain: Carpet area = Inner dimensions. (9.7-0.3) x (14.7-0.3) = 9.4 x 14.4 = 135.36 m^2.

q: 17. In the centre line method of working out volumes, for cross walls, what deductions must be made from the centre line length at each junction?
explain: In the centre-line method, since the centre-line automatically accounts for corners of the main wall, a deduction of half the breadth of the cross (partition) wall is made at each junction to avoid double counting.

q: 18. Pick up the item of work not included in the plinth area estimate
explain: An open courtyard is not a covered/built-up space, so its area is excluded from the plinth area estimate, unlike wall thickness, room area, and covered verandah area.

q: 19. The useful part of liveable area of a building is also known as
explain: Carpet area is the actual usable/liveable floor area within a building, excluding wall thickness and common circulation spaces.

q: 20. The process of evaluating cost of construction of a project is called
explain: The overall process of evaluating and calculating the probable cost of a construction project before it begins is called estimating.

q: 21. The essential requirements to prepare a good estimate are
options: a full dimensioned drawing to scale
explain: A good, reliable estimate requires a fully dimensioned scaled drawing, detailed specifications of materials/workmanship, and an appropriate schedule of rates -- all three together.

q: 22. The necessary elements of an estimates are
explain: A complete estimate needs drawings (for quantities), specifications (for quality/method), and rates (for pricing) — all three elements together.

q: 23. Tentative cost of a road project is calculated by
explain: Preliminary or tentative estimates for roads are usually prepared on a 'per kilometer' or 'per meter' length basis.

q: 24. Which one area must be greater at any floor of a building?
explain: Plinth area is the largest as it includes the floor area plus the area occupied by the walls.

q: 25. The investment required for the completion of any project is obtained by
explain: Estimating provides the probable cost, which informs the investment or budget needed before the project starts.

q: 26. Which one is correct with respect to floor area and plinth area?
options: floor area is always greater than plinth area
floor area is always equal to plinth area
floor area is always lesser than plinth area
explain: Floor area is the plinth area minus the area occupied by the walls, hence it is always smaller.

q: 27. Which of the following estimates, which most accurately reflect the actual cost of the project?
explain: Bottom-up estimating builds the total cost from detailed individual components upward, making it the most accurate reflection of actual project cost.

q: 28. The capacity of septic tank for 10 users will be roughly
explain: For a small household of about 10 users, the required septic tank capacity works out to roughly 7 to 8 cubic metres, based on standard per-capita sewage flow and retention norms.

q: 29. Which is not the standard method of calculating quantities?
options: long wall and short wall method
explain: The 'crossing method' is not a recognized standard method of quantity calculation; the recognized methods are long wall-short wall, centre line, and plinth area methods.

q: 30. Which of the following is the most correct estimate?
explain: A detailed estimate, prepared item-by-item from actual quantities and current rates, is the most accurate/correct type of estimate among those listed.

q: 31. Find the area of the quadrilateral shown below and dimension are in m (Diagonal 70, offsets 50 and 40)
explain: Area of quadrilateral = 0.5 * diagonal * (sum of offsets) = 0.5 * 70 * (50 + 40) = 35 * 90 = 3150 m². *Note: The answer key indicates 'd' (2450) based on potentially different image interpretation or key error*.

q: 32. For the cost estimation of a building project at concept-development phase; the method used is
explain: At the early concept-development phase, cost estimation relies on assumptions based on similar previously executed projects, since detailed drawings are not yet available.

q: 33. The total estimated cost of a building electrification usually accounts for
explain: Building electrification cost is generally taken as approximately 8% of the total building construction estimate.

q: 34. Due to change in price level, a revised estimate is prepared if the sanctioned estimate exceeds:
explain: A revised estimate becomes necessary when actual/anticipated costs exceed the sanctioned estimate by more than 5%, often due to price escalation.

q: 35. Centre line method of estimation is mostly used for
explain: The centre line method is most commonly used for building works, especially where wall layouts are regular and symmetrical.

q: 36. The plinth area method is also known as
explain: The plinth area method of estimating (cost = plinth area × rate per unit area) is also commonly known as the square rate method.

q: 37. Carpet area does not include the area of
options: the walls along with doors and other openings
explain: Carpet area is the strictly usable/liveable floor area, so it excludes wall thickness with openings, verandah/corridor/passage space, and bathroom/lavatory area -- all of the listed items are excluded.

q: 38. In the detailed estimate the areas are worked out to the nearest
explain: As a standard estimating precision, areas in a detailed estimate are worked out correct to the nearest 0.01 m².

q: 39. Pick up the correct statement regarding the centre line method of estimating a building
options: product of the centre line of the walls and area of cross-section of any item, gives total quantity of the item
the centre line is worked out separately for different sections of walls of a building
the centre line length is reduced by half the layer of main wall joining the partition wall
explain: In the centre-line method, the total quantity is obtained by multiplying centre-line length by cross-sectional area, the centre line is worked out separately for different wall sections, and adjustments (reductions) are made where partition walls join main walls -- all these statements are true.

q: 40. The 'centre line method' is specially adopted for estimating
explain: The centre-line method is particularly suited for estimating buildings with circular, hexagonal, or octagonal plan shapes, since it simplifies the otherwise complex geometry into a single centre-line calculation.

q: 41. Which of the following factor is a reason for need to provided for contingency in the cost estimate of a project?
explain: A contingency provision is included in a cost estimate specifically to cover uncertainty -- unforeseen items or price variations that cannot be precisely predicted at the estimation stage.
